milestone: S9a: a Debug Adapter Protocol server, sniff --dap, on Linux x86-64
scope: S9a's rows: the base protocol and its envelope (U1), sessions over the S2 command set on Linux (U2), and attach by process id, a core file and the remote kernel (U3). macOS and PAX are predicted in their own file when their PR starts.

measured_before_code.gdb: the pinned gdb 15.1 in DAP mode (gdb -i=dap), run only as a binary over thirteen rows, two takes each, over gcc's and clang's session builds: every row that ran agreed between its takes after the named normalisations. It declares 23 capabilities; it starts the program at launch and answers configurationDone with notStopped after breakpoints; it refuses threads with notStopped while the program runs; pause stops with reason pause; stopAtBeginningOfMainSubprogram stops in main; stopOnEntry is ignored; evaluate in the repl context answers the command's text
measured_before_code.lldb-dap: Apple's lldb-dap (LLVM 21.0.0), the same thirteen rows on macOS: twelve agreed between takes, and stopAtBeginningOfMainSubprogram is ignored there; stopOnEntry and pause stop with reason exception, signal SIGSTOP; it declares 22 capabilities, 19 in common with gdb's
measured_before_code.normalisations: seq and request_seq; thread, frame, variablesReference, breakpoint and memoryReference ids and systemProcessId, each by first appearance; addresses and process ids in text; module and loadedSource events not compared; responses compared in request order and other events in their own order

surface.entry: sniff --dap, over standard input and output only
surface.launch: program, args, cwd, env and stopAtBeginningOfMainSubprogram, as gdb names them; stopOnEntry refused by name
surface.attach: pid, target or coreFile, checked in that order
surface.repl: evaluate in the repl context runs one line of the command language and answers its text
surface.extensions: none: a request sniff does not support is answered success: false, naming it

named_differences.launch-start: gdb 15.1 starts the program at launch and answers configurationDone notStopped after breakpoints; sniff starts it at configurationDone and answers success: true, following the specification and the CLI twin (break before run)
named_differences.threads-running: threads while the program runs is refused notStopped, as gdb (the Linux oracle) answers; the thread id comes from the thread event with reason started
named_differences.capabilities: sniff's capabilities object is held to its own declared set, not to gdb's

compilers: each C row runs over gcc's and clang's session builds (@CC@), as the measurement did

rows.name: dap-frame-refusals
rows.does: no Content-Length; a length that is not a number or is negative; a header line over 4,096 bytes; more than 32 header fields; a body over 64 MiB; a body that is not JSON; a body that is not UTF-8; the input ends inside a body
rows.oracle: the specification (overview's base protocol, the schema)
rows.prediction: each refused by its own name, the reader then dead; never a crash
